newsitem.title: GREECE: Greece hesitant to recall ambassador to Iran.
newsitem.headline: Greece hesitant to recall ambassador to Iran.

text.p: Greece expressed reservations on Friday about a European Union appeal to recall EU ambassadors from Tehran after a German court accused Iranian political leaders of ordering the murder of Kurdish dissidents in Berlin.

Although Greece was staunchly opposed to terrorism and the use of violence, it found that isolating a country was not the best way to bring it into the international family, government spokesman Dimitris Reppas said.
"Under this light, we express reservations for the necessity of this measure, to withdraw the ambassadors from the Iranian capital. We are still examining the issue," he told reporters.
The presidency of the European Union appealed to EU members to show solidarity with Germany by ordering their ambassadors to Iran home for consultations.
The EU action followed a German court finding on Thursday that senior Iranian leaders ordered the killings of a group of Iranian Kurdish leaders in a Berlin restaurant in 1992.
In Bonn, the German Foreign Ministry expressed its astonishment at Greece's decision.
"We have taken note of the fact that Greece, as the only EU country, has decided not to take part in European solidarity with astonishment and surprise," the spokesman said.
